name: Zibeon
overview: Zibeon is a male Edomite figure noted in Scripture as the son of Seir and a chief in Edom, marking him as a significant leader within the Edomite tribe. His identity is firmly rooted in the genealogical records of Genesis, highlighting his role within the lineage of Edomites. There are no additional notes expanding on his life or character beyond these details.
namesAndTitles: The name Zibeon means 'hyena,' which is a proper name mentioned in Genesis 36:20. This meaning is not indicated as given by God, but it reflects the Hebrew naming tradition recorded in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Zibeon as the son of Seir. Additionally, there are inferred paternal relationships linking him to Aiah and Beeri, suggesting a broader family context within the Edomite genealogy. Beyond these, no further family relationships are detailed in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Zibeon's significance in the biblical narrative lies primarily in his role as a chief in Edom and as a descendant of Seir, situating him within the historical and tribal framework of the Edomites. His mention in Genesis 36 emphasizes the genealogical and leadership structures important to understanding the lineage and governance of Edom. While the text does not elaborate on his personal deeds, his position as a chief underscores his importance in the ancestral history of this people group.
